solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Motor-racing company accepting a second disaster

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: F1, Formula One, with the digit read as the letter I
CO is the standard abbreviation for company
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A racing team taking on a second outfit ends in calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motor-racing company' reads as one firm, but it splits: F1 for the sport and CO for company, with A and S slotted between them to give FIASCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating failure, a complete shambles, which is exactly what a disaster can mean in everyday speech.

clue.text: Bar manager from sounding out popular goalie

indicators.note: sounding something out means saying it aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the result

blocks.note: something popular is in, as in fashion
a goalkeeper, keeper for short
the two words run together say the same as a pub landlord's title

explanation.surface: Someone who runs a bar takes their name from the call of a favourite goalkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: IN plus KEEPER, said aloud, is INNKEEPER; the spelling gains the second N of 'inn'.
explanation.definitionFit: An innkeeper runs a pub or inn, so is the person in charge of a bar and its drinks trade.

clue.text: Radio announcement’s to recognise a worry: coastal fog

indicators.note: on the radio you only hear words, so what follows is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: to see something can mean to recognise or understand it
a fret is a state of worry
the first part sounds like the word for the ocean

explanation.surface: A weather bulletin announces the need to watch out for fog along the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: SEE plus FRET, spoken, sounds like SEA FRET. A sea fret is a cold mist that rolls in off the North Sea onto England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a damp mist drifting inland from the sea, a regional British name for fog by the shore.

clue.text: Individual going East

blocks.note: something going, or running, is on
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A lone person heads off eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' looks like travel towards the East, but it means 'on', as a machine or show that is going is on.
explanation.definitionFit: One means a single person or thing, the same sense as an individual standing alone.

clue.text: GP, say, keeping various items around the house

indicators.note: various suggests things in assorted forms, so the letters come in a different order
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a GP, general practitioner, is an example of a doctor, or doc
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A family doctor has a collection of household objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks a GP as one example of a doctor. 'Around the house' reads as part of the wordplay but is the definition, used adjectivally.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic describes things to do with the home and household, so domestic chores are jobs done in and about the home.

clue.text: Contract excluding wife’s tax

indicators.note: to exclude something is to leave it out, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to draw in is to contract or pull inward
W is the abbreviation for wife, as used in family trees and records of marital status

explanation.surface: A deal that keeps a spouse out of a tax arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a legal agreement, but it is a verb meaning shrink: DRAW IN, and taking the W away leaves DRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax as a verb can mean to strain or exhaust resources, the same sense as draining one's energy.

clue.text: One with particular interest in offering ready supply

definitions.text: One with particular interest in offering ready supply

blocks.clueFragment: One with particular interest in offering ready supply
blocks.note: surface reading: someone keen and eager to help out with provisions
setter's reading: interest is the charge on a loan, and ready is slang for cash, so this is someone supplying cash for interest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Interest' seems to mean enthusiasm, but it is the charge on a loan, and 'the ready' or 'readies' is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender advances cash to borrowers and profits from the interest charged, so supplying ready money is the whole business.

clue.text: Singer, very good, keeping musical work organised

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: 'so!' is an old interjection of approval meaning 'very good, that will do'
OP is the abbreviation for opus, a numbered musical work
to run something is to organise it

explanation.surface: A talented singer is staging a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' looks like an anagram signal, but it supplies letters as a past tense meaning managed. 'So!' as approval is old-fashioned but in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a female or boy singer with the highest vocal range, so a type of singer.

clue.text: Useless writer is shown up in it

indicators.note: in a down clue, something pushed upward reads from bottom to top
being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hopeless author gets exposed by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shown up' suggests embarrassment, but in a down entry it means turned upward; the writer is a pen, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or competence, so someone inept is useless at the task in hand.

clue.text: In time to keep river out of public view

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the outer piece holds the inner

blocks.note: taken as written
the Cam is the river through Cambridge
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Diverting a river quietly, away from the public gaze.
explanation.walkthrough: IN ERA is opened up to hold CAM, the Cambridge river.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal Latin phrase for proceedings held in private, with press and public excluded.

clue.text: European city that never sleeps? Not quite

indicators.note: something not quite complete falls short at the end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: never taking a nap means being without one

explanation.surface: Is this the European city that never sleeps? Not really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The city that never sleeps' is New York's nickname, which tempts a wrong answer; here it is NAPLESS, one letter too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a large port city in southern Italy, so it is a European city.

clue.text: City and Italian city-dweller about to appear in US city? Magic

indicators.note: appearing in something means being found inside it

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district
someone who lives in Rome
C stands for circa, Latin for about
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A Londoner and a Roman turn up in an American city and perform magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' with a capital C is the financial district of London, known by its postcode; the US city is split open to take everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromancy is sorcery, especially conjuring the dead, so it is a form of black magic or witchcraft.

clue.text: Decorator’s accessory: staff retaining piece to copy

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one thing ends up held inside another

blocks.note: a mast is a pole, as in a flagstaff
the king is a chess piece
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: A painter's essential: workers keeping a sample to reproduce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees, but it means a pole, and 'piece' is a chess piece rather than a scrap of material.
explanation.definitionFit: Masking tape is the paper sticky tape painters lay along edges to keep paint off surfaces nearby.

clue.text: Cultured person losing head

indicators.note: losing the head means the front is cut off, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: in legal language a party is a person involved in a case or contract

explanation.surface: A refined individual loses their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultured person' looks like the definition, but only 'Cultured' is; 'person' is PARTY, as in 'the guilty party'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means showing interest in the arts, often a little pretentiously, a looser word for refined or cultivated.

clue.text: Recalled best mark

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so it runs the opposite way

blocks.note: the tops is slang for the best

explanation.surface: Remembering the highest grade awarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' suggests memory, but it means turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or stain, so the two words are interchangeable for a blemish.

clue.text: Opening for Surrey, vital to get on this?

definitions.text: Opening for Surrey, vital to get on this?

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the start of the word is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the county
core describes something central or essential, as in core values
to board is to get on a vehicle

explanation.surface: Surrey's opening batsman needs to get his runs posted on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county cricket side, and an opener must get runs on the board; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoreboard displays the runs at a cricket ground, the place an opening batsman wants to see his total appear.

clue.text: Bird that hurts gerbil’s tail

indicators.note: a tail is the end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: 'ow!' is what you say when something hurts
the final letter of the rodent's name

explanation.surface: A bird of prey gives a gerbil a painful nip on its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That hurts' is the cry itself, OW.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is a nocturnal bird of prey, which happens to hunt small rodents.

clue.text: Think back regarding main road south into French city

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: re means regarding, about
the M1, Britain's first motorway, with the digit read as I
Nice is a city on the French Riviera
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Recalling a drive south down the motorway into a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, its digit read as the letter I; the French city is the one on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past experiences fondly, so it means remembering or looking back.

clue.text: High-minded headmaster dismissing a limited version of education?

indicators.note: to dismiss is to send away, so a letter leaves
a limited version is cut short, so the word is clipped to its start

blocks.note: a principal is the head of a school or college
taken as written
ED is the common short form of education

explanation.surface: A lofty-minded head teacher scraps a narrow curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dismissing' fits the headmaster sacking someone, but it removes the A from PRINCIPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Principled means guided by firm moral standards, close to high-minded or acting on ideals.

clue.text: New expedition from east of London to secure Kentish garden centre?

indicators.note: East End Londoners traditionally drop their aitches, so the H falls away
to secure something is to hold it firmly, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
expedition can mean speed or haste
Kent is a county in South East England

explanation.surface: A fresh trip out from London to visit a Kent garden centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey, but it means haste; a Cockney says 'urry. Kent is the 'Garden of England', which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a place where plants are raised and sold, essentially what a garden centre is; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Horse covering miles in search

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so the outer piece goes round the inner

blocks.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A horse travels many miles looking for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering miles' suggests a horse travelling a distance, but it means the horse surrounds M.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as if dragging a comb's teeth through it.

clue.text: Difficult enough after losing answer in guide

indicators.note: once something is lost it is gone, so a letter drops out
being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: a cox steers and guides a rowing boat
ample means plenty, enough
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A hard enough clue once you have lost the answer in the guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' is the person who steers a rowing boat. 'Answer' is A, as in Q and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Complex means made of many intricate parts, and so hard to understand, close to difficult or complicated.

clue.text: Acclaim, losing no time

indicators.note: when something is lost it is taken away, so letters are removed

blocks.note: to acclaim someone is to honour them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise given promptly, without wasting a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing no time' reads as 'quickly', but it splits: the word 'no' is lost, and 'time' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time, sixty minutes long, so it is a specific example of a time period.

clue.text: Disapprobation over simple-minded besieging University

indicators.note: an army besieging a town surrounds it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
dim means slow-witted
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Contempt for dim-witted people laying siege to a university.
explanation.walkthrough: O comes first, then DIM surrounds U.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust directed at someone, a strong form of public condemnation.

clue.text: Great to keep remaining Northern soldiers in control

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the outer piece holds the others

blocks.note: GT is the abbreviation for great
something left over is remaining
N is the abbreviation for northern
ordinary soldiers are often called men

explanation.surface: A general holds back his remaining northern troops while staying in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: GT is opened up to hold OVER, N and MEN in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Government means the act of ruling or managing, as in good government, so it is a synonym of control.

clue.text: Promoter of diet, say, in the forefront

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the front of an army or movement
e.g. means 'for example', which is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A diet campaigner leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The forefront' is the vanguard, shortened in crosswords to its first syllable; 'say' is the usual signal for an example abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan follows and often champions a plant-based eating plan, so is an advocate for one particular way of eating.

clue.text: Theater, the last word in comfort originally, heading west

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the beginning, so only starting letters are taken
in an across entry, travelling west means moving right to left

blocks.note: amen is the word said at the end of a prayer
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An American theatre, the ultimate in comfort, moves out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' takes the first letters of both 'in' and 'comfort'. The American spelling 'Theater' hints at a movie theater.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English a movie theater is what Britons call a cinema, the building where films are shown.

clue.text: Uncontrollable oil gush — hot and revolting

indicators.note: something out of control runs wild, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A blowout at an oil well spews hot, disgusting crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' joins the oil gush in the mix; 'revolting' is an adjective here, not rebelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghoulish means morbidly fascinated by death or horror, and so gruesome and disgusting to others.

clue.text: Unconscious in fight, getting head struck

indicators.note: striking off the head removes the front, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a bout is a boxing match

explanation.surface: A boxer knocked senseless after a blow to the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head struck' sounds like a punch, but it means the first letter of BOUT is struck off.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer who is out cold has been knocked senseless, so out can mean unconscious.

clue.text: Call back about fire in the sky

indicators.note: going back means moving the opposite way
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to call someone something is to name them
a pyre is a heap of wood burnt as a funeral fire

explanation.surface: Someone shouts again about a blaze up in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call back' reads as phoning someone back, but it is a word for call written backwards, wrapped about a funeral fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The empyrean is the highest heaven in old cosmology, so poetically it means the heavens or firmament above.

clue.text: Time with former lovers consuming Frenchman’s cuisine

indicators.note: to consume is to take inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
two exes, each an ex being a former partner
M is short for Monsieur, the French for Mr

explanation.surface: Spending time with ex-partners who are eating a Frenchman's cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: The exes are two separate EX chunks, and M goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tex-Mex is the Texan take on Mexican food, so it is a style of cooking, a regional cuisine.
